title: a layer providing some other capability does not satisfy a row a coercion member introduced; the provide is refused naming the capability the member reads
notes: specification/requirements.mdx, 'Satisfaction': 'Providing a layer to a computation MUST remove matching capabilities from the computation's unsatisfied requirement row' and 'When the compiler knows the complete closure, an unsatisfied capability MUST be a compile error.' The body here coerces three objects whose members read Db, and the layer supplies Log. Nothing matches, so nothing is subtracted, and the provide must be refused for Db. WHY THIS CASE EXISTS SEPARATELY FROM THE ACCEPTING ONE: a green `output` case proves a program was not refused, which is a weaker statement than it looks. A backend that charged NO row at all for a coercion also produces a green `output` case — the body needs nothing, so the layer satisfies it vacuously — and that is exactly the fail-open the coercion work of 2026-08-27 closed. This case is what makes the accepting sibling mean something: with the wrong layer, a backend that recorded no row still compiles the program and this case goes red. It is the only shape in the corpus that distinguishes 'the row was recorded and subtracted' from 'there was never a row'. `messageContains` is declared and the payload IS the promise: `SMITHERS2101` at this position is satisfied by a refusal naming Log — the capability that WAS supplied — which is precisely what a backend that computed the provided and required sets the wrong way round would say, and it would be a different program's diagnostic passing this expectation. The fragment is the bare capability name rather than a rendered row, because the reference prints `Db` where the fork prints `{Db}`. WHAT THIS CASE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT PIN: a `SMITHERS2102`. There is no top-level call with an unsatisfied row here — the calls are inside the provide body — so the top-level rule does not fire, and declaring it would ratify a cascade neither backend produces. It also deliberately uses only three of the eight spellings its sibling runs: the point is that the row TRAVELS, which one spelling would establish, and three is enough to show it is not an artifact of one member kind while keeping the case's failure legible. VERIFIED LOAD-BEARING, not assumed: mutating the declared `messageContains` from `Db` to `Log` turns the case red on BOTH backends with the message diff printed, and the file was restored byte-identically (sha256 f19129498233bd2301175f9a04a511816b2f7603fecd1f92279cb037af3c728f before and after, that digest being this file's content at the moment the mutation ran — the sentence recording it is appended afterwards, so the shipped file necessarily hashes differently). The paired positive control is `the-coercion-row-reaches-the-provide-site-and-runs`, the same shape with the RIGHT layer, which must keep compiling AND RUNNING.
